title: The Hanged Man and the "Only Trust Your Heart" title mix-up
summary: He scored the TV film The Hanged Man; his song with Sammy Cahn lyrics was wrongly credited because of an identical title.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: What about "The Hanged One" ... in that film?
You mean "The Hanged Man".
"The Hanged Man", yes.
That was -- that's right, well, that was still a film for TV, wasn't it -- at Universal? Yes, I did that.
You did the background?
Yes. I did the complete picture, yes.
Who was in that?
Oh, Broderick Crawford ... I think, Robert Culp, Vera Miles.
Uh huh. Where did, or how did your tune, "Only Trust Your Heart" get written? Did that have to do first with a TV show, or ...
Yes, that was for a TV show ... what was that? Was that over at 20th?
"It Takes a Thief" or "Fame is the Name" or something.
Oh no, that came from "The Hanged Man".
"The Hanged Man".
Yeah, that came from the "Hanged Man", yes.
Was Astrud Gilberto in that?
In a nightclub scene, with the Stan Getz quartet.
I see.
Yes, that's right. And following that, they recorded it.
And she just appeared -- she was not a character in the story, was she?
No, no. She just appeared as a singer in the club.
Uh huh.
An interesting thing about that song, "Only Trust Your Heart" -- I don't know that I've told you about that before, but Sammy Cahn wrote the lyrics to that song.
Yes.

And when the first record came out in the album, it listed as composer Nicholas Bronsky, Nicholas Bronsky and Sammy Cahn -- and when I saw this, I got in touch immediately with the studio, and wanted to know what had happened here. And I was told that they didn't really know, but that they would look into it.
Well, they got back to me, and what they discovered

was that Sammy Cahn has, inadvertently, of course, written, or used the same title that he had used for another song, with which, you know, that he had collaborated with Nicholas Bronsky on. And I don't know how labeling or programming or whoever the people at the record company could have gotten his name on it, because they would certainly have received the music, you know, from my own song. I would think so -- or maybe they just took the title and just looked it up in the ASCAP files or something and said, "Well, Bronsky and Cahn".

But Sammy had forgotten that he had written another song by this title. Noe he's a very prolific writer, as we know -- but the funny thing about it was I dismissed it then; I said, "Well, it's probably some little insignificant song that they wrote" -- and never did anything with more.

And then just a few months ago, I was looking at late television and I don't know why I happened to look at a picture called "Ten Thousand Bedrooms" with Dean Martin -- and here's this song, "Only Trust Your Heart". But of course, it's the Nicholas Bronsky melody, and the other Sammy Cahn lyric. But the only thing that's the same about our song is the title.
Is the lyric on the same theme?
I don't remember the lyric, because I don't even remember what the song sounded like. As a matter of fact, I think that what happened, if I heard the song, I
probably didn't hear it sung --but in the credits at the end, I saw the song, "Only Trust Your Heart" by Nicholas Bronsky and Sammy Cahn. And I said, "Ah, that's it!"
Well, there's a lot of repetition in these things, but also I didn't realize in the titles, even.
Well, I have two songs called "Once Upon a Time".
That's right.

But the second one is called "Once Upon a Time It Happened " -- and that was because the lyricist, you know, wrote -- used that title for the song, not knowing that I had another song called "Once Upon a Time" --and Dean Martin liked the song, and recorded it.
Does Ed know that -- about his recording of it?
Oh, I think so. Yes.
Oh, he must.
Yes.
